hero.lede: A neighborhood grill built around one oak-fed hearth — steaks, roasted vegetables, and flatbreads cooked the same way for eight years running.

story.heading: One hearth, one neighborhood
paragraphs: Ember & Oak started as a single wood-fired hearth in a converted garage bay, three blocks from where it stands now. There was no gas line, no fryer, no flat-top — just oak, iron, and whatever came off the grill that night.

Eight years later, that's still the whole kitchen. Every dish that leaves it has touched the fire at some point, whether that means a forty-minute low roast or a ninety-second blister right over the coals. We buy whole animals from three farms within sixty miles and change the menu with what shows up.
story.quote: "We don't have a fryer. We don't have a microwave. If it can't be done over oak, it's not on the menu."

items.text: "The ribeye alone is worth the drive across town. Smoky in a way that actually tastes like wood, not liquid smoke."
items.author: Priya M. — regular since 2019

items.text: "Brought my whole family for a birthday and the half chicken disappeared in ten minutes flat. Book ahead on weekends."
items.author: Tom H. — Northside resident

items.text: "Best vegetarian option in the area that doesn't feel like an afterthought. The cauliflower steak is a full meal."
